headline.technical: Asian equities rebounded on 26 Nov as investors shrugged off new US tariff proposals (WSJ, CNBC); Nasdaq is still 1m -10.92% and the VIX closed at 28.29.
headline.layman: Asian stock markets bounced back today even after the US proposed new import taxes. Tech shares are still well below where they were a month ago.

global.title: Asia rebounds on tech; AI worries and tariffs linger

status.technical: WSJ reported Asian stocks staged a comeback after a selloff as investors shrugged off US tariff proposals. The Nasdaq closed 1d -0.62%, 5d -3.46%; the VIX closed at 28.29.
status.layman: Asian markets recovered after a sell-off. Wall Street ended lower but well above its lows. The VIX, a gauge of market nervousness, closed at 28.29.

consequence.technical: If AI-sustainability fears return (the FT noted tech shares were hit this month by such fears), volatility could stay elevated; if the tech rebound holds, risk appetite may stabilise.
consequence.layman: If worries about the AI boom come back, markets could stay jumpy. If the tech rebound holds, nerves may settle.

impact.technical: Bloomberg/WSJ reported hedge fund Situational Awareness told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter on highly levered AI bets, a sign of concentration risk.
impact.layman: One hedge fund that made big borrowed bets on AI companies told investors it lost 65% in the third quarter.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of 825 times and over the next 5 days 59% of 824 times.
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast: after calm days like this, the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of the time.

regions.title: Americas: Wall Street AI selloff, US tariffs on Brazil

status.technical: The Dow rose 0.33% while the Nasdaq fell 0.62% as an AI selloff hit Wall Street (BusinessLine). Reuters reported the US proposed new tariffs on Brazil, including a 10% duty on aircraft; Bovespa closed 1d 1.58%.
status.layman: On Wall Street the Dow rose but the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell on AI worries. The US proposed new import taxes on Brazil, including 10% on aircraft.

consequence.technical: Brazil's president's office said it will not yield to threats and aims for a negotiated resolution (Al Jazeera); if talks happen, tariff risk could ease. Bloomberg reported Lula sounded out Bradesco's Luiz Trabuco about joining his government.
consequence.layman: Brazil says it won't give in but wants to negotiate. If talks work, the tariff worry could fade.

impact.technical: Brazilian aircraft exporters face the proposed duty (Reuters). The Bovespa sits at a drawdown from its 52-week high of -20.27%.
impact.layman: Brazilian aircraft makers would be hit by the proposed tax. Brazil's main stock index is well below its yearly high.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 845 times and over the next 5 days 59% of 844 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days, the S&P 500 rose over the next five days 59% of the time.

regions.title: Europe: lower close, UK inflation and Germany-France gap

status.technical: The Euro Stoxx 50 closed 1d -1.82%, the DAX -1.26% and the FTSE 100 -0.38%. WSJ reported German growth at its strongest in more than four years while France struggled to grow.
status.layman: European stocks fell on Wednesday. Germany's economy is growing faster, while France's is struggling.

consequence.technical: WSJ reported UK inflation rose as energy costs keep pressure on the Bank of England; the BOE's Bailey sees the length of the Iran war as key to the rate path.
consequence.layman: UK prices are rising. The Bank of England's next move depends partly on how long the Iran war lasts.

impact.technical: WSJ reported French real wages are falling as inflation rises, fuelling protests; UK households face higher energy costs.
impact.layman: French households are losing buying power, which is fuelling protests.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 52% of 161 times and over the next 5 days 55% of 159 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after big down days, European stocks rose over the next five days a bit more than half the time (55%).

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: tech-led rebound, Bank of Korea hikes

status.technical: Kospi closed 1d 1.74%, TAIEX 3.15%, Nikkei 1.51% and Hang Seng 1.86%. CNBC reported Kospi led gains on a tech rebound; the Bank of Korea raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.25%.
status.layman: Asian stocks rose, led by South Korea's tech shares. South Korea's central bank raised interest rates to 3.25%.

consequence.technical: WSJ reported BOJ's Tamura urged timely rate hikes, bolstering the case for a December move; if the BOJ tightens, yen and JGB yields could be affected.
consequence.layman: A Bank of Japan official wants rate increases soon. If they happen, the yen and Japanese bond yields could move.

impact.technical: Bloomberg reported Japan protested a 15% levy; Singapore is 'very disappointed' (Straits Times). CNBC said proposed 18% and 20% tariffs on rival exporters could give India an edge.
impact.layman: Japan and Singapore object to the proposed US tariffs. India may gain a competitive edge over some rival exporters.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days Kospi rose the next day 55% of 823 times and over the next 5 days 57% of 823 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days, South Korea's Kospi rose over the next five days 57% of the time.

status.technical: CNBC reported the White House unveiled tariffs targeting more than a dozen major trading partners. Straits Times reported two-thirds of American voters in exit polls said the duties have hurt the national economy.
status.layman: The US proposed new import taxes on more than a dozen trading partners. Many US voters in exit polls say tariffs have hurt the economy.

consequence.technical: Singapore will urge Washington to reconsider (Bloomberg) and the US left the door open to a lower deal (Straits Times); if talks succeed, final rates could differ from proposals.
consequence.layman: Countries are asking the US to rethink. If deals are reached, final taxes could be lower than proposed.

impact.technical: Jefferies, cited by Business Standard, noted a significant portion of India's $104 billion annual exports to the US remains outside the current tariff framework or is subject to sector-specific levies.
impact.layman: Jefferies says a large part of India's exports to the US is not covered by these new tariffs.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose over the next 5 days 59% of 844 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days, the S&P 500 rose over the next five days 59% of the time.

status.technical: FT reported tech shares were hit this month by fears over whether the AI boom can be sustained. Business Standard reported Nvidia ended down 3.9% at $149.30 on Wednesday.
status.layman: Worries about whether the AI boom can last have hit tech shares this month. Nvidia fell 3.9% on Wednesday.

consequence.technical: Straits Times reported billions in data centre deals have ground to a halt after AI chip curbs; if funding stays scarce, AI-linked spending could slow.
consequence.layman: Some big data-centre deals have stalled after new chip limits. If that continues, AI spending could slow.

impact.technical: S&P Global Ratings said Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch, citing 'rising' management and governance risk (CNBC). Evidence beyond Nvidia is thin.
impact.layman: S&P warned it could lower Nvidia's credit rating because of management and governance concerns.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of 825 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days, the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of the time.

status.technical: CNBC reported the Fed's preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October. Economic Times reported upcoming indicators hint at potential Fed rate increases in December; the 10-year yield closed 4.85, 1d -1.14%.
status.layman: A key US inflation gauge rose to 3.8% in October. Traders think the Fed may raise rates in December.

consequence.technical: If inflation stays high, then rate-hike bets could persist; Economic Times reported hot US inflation cemented Fed hike bets and weighed on gold.
consequence.layman: If prices keep rising, rate hikes become more likely, which has weighed on gold.

impact.technical: Rate-hike bets weigh on bullion (Economic Times); gold closed 1d 1.78% but is -22.27% over 3 months.
impact.layman: Higher expected interest rates have made gold less attractive; it is still far below where it was three months ago.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises bigger than 1 standard deviation, gold rose over the next 5 days 58% of 191 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after big gold gains, gold rose over the next five days 58% of the time.

status.technical: Business Standard reported Brent crude futures were 10 cents, or 0.1%, higher at $94.71 a barrel after Iran claimed mine strikes on ships. WSJ reported Iran's economy is straining under a US blockade.
status.layman: Oil edged up after Iran claimed attacks on ships. Iran's economy is under strain from a US blockade.

consequence.technical: BOE's Bailey sees the length of the Iran war as key to the rate path (WSJ); if the conflict lasts, energy costs could keep inflation pressure on central banks.
consequence.layman: If the Iran conflict drags on, energy costs could keep prices high.

impact.technical: Mint reported softer crude helped Indian shares, and Economic Times said falling oil prices supported the rupee. Evidence on other markets is thin.
impact.layman: Cheaper oil helped Indian stocks and the rupee.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days Brent rose over the next 5 days 51% of 844 times.
outlook.layman: History, not a forecast: after calm days, oil rose over the next five days about half the time (51%).

events.title: US Thanksgiving holiday
events.technical: WSJ noted Wall Street recouped most of its sharp losses ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
events.layman: US markets recovered most of their losses before the Thanksgiving holiday.

events.title: Black Friday shopping
events.technical: CNBC reported K-beauty brands topping Amazon skincare rankings ahead of Black Friday, lifting South Korean beauty stocks.
events.layman: Korean beauty brands are selling well online before Black Friday, and their shares rose.

companyEffects.technical: Nvidia ended down 3.9% at $149.30 on Wednesday (Business Standard); S&P Global Ratings said its credit rating could be cut by one notch (CNBC).
companyEffects.layman: Nvidia fell 3.9% on Wednesday and S&P warned it could lower the company's credit rating.

companyEffects.technical: Economic Times reported Alphabet shares plunged over 5% amid AI investment concerns, regulatory challenges and broader technology weakness.
companyEffects.layman: Alphabet's shares dropped sharply on AI spending worries and other concerns.

companyEffects.technical: SCMP reported a production cut sent CATL's market capitalisation below the 1 trillion yuan mark; analysts expect weak battery demand to keep weighing.
companyEffects.layman: China's battery giant CATL has fallen in value on worries about weak demand.
